title: ASDF: A Compiler for Qwerty, a Basis-Oriented Quantum Programming Language
problem: Compiling basis-oriented quantum languages requires synthesizing circuits from basis translations and automatically specializing adjoint or predicated function forms, challenging existing circuit-oriented compilation approaches.
motivation: Higher-level quantum programming paradigms built on bases and functions offer improved programmer productivity but require novel compilation techniques distinct from circuit-oriented approaches.
method: ASDF implements a high-level quantum IR using MLIR framework, enabling basis translation to circuit synthesis and automatic specialization of adjoint/predicated functions. Produces OpenQASM 3 or QIR output for simulation or hardware execution, with gate cost comparable to circuit-oriented compilers.
key_novelty: Novel high-level quantum IR in MLIR specifically designed for basis-oriented quantum languages, enabling efficient synthesis from higher-level abstractions.
contributions: First compiler for basis-oriented quantum programming languages
High-level quantum IR implemented in MLIR framework
Automatic basis translation to circuit generation
Comparable fault-tolerant resource requirements to circuit-oriented approaches

metrics.other: Comparable fault-tolerant resource cost to prior compilers

limitations: Evaluation limited to fault-tolerant resource comparison; runtime performance and optimization techniques not discussed.
primary_theme: Basis-oriented quantum compiler with MLIR IR
